title: League of Legends Patch 26.21 Notes
description: True Damage has arrived with style! Plus tons to look forward to across SR, Mayhem, Classic, and Arena.

entries.context: This patch we did work to adjust Varus' top and bottom power skew, which involved shifting the balance between his Q and W for laning. While the resulting changes have seemed promising, we unfortunately added a major bug to his Q during this work, causing it to no longer deal reduced damage to subsequent targets. We are fixing that bug, and compensating with a buff.

changes.text: Passive Bonus AD and AP on Kill/Takedown: (1.1 per 10% AS) as bonus AD and AP ⇒ 1.4 per 10% AS
changes.label: Passive Bonus AD and AP on Kill/Takedown
changes.before: (1.1 per 10% AS) as bonus AD and AP

entries.context: Starting during Patch 26.21, replay downloads will be limited to 10 per hour. You will still be able to download your own replays, as well as replays from your friends and other players. This change is necessary to prevent large-scale abuse of downloaded replays by bad actors using vibecoded apps to scrape thousands upon thousands of replays. We opted for a time-based limit to still allow creators to make content, while preventing mass exploitative downloads. We’ll continue to monitor how many replays are downloaded to ensure players have access to this important feature while preventing clear misuse.

entries.name: Azir
entries.context: We've kept the Emperor of the Sands’ mana pool pretty dry to make sure he needs to use soldier attacks properly for lane control early instead of just spamming [Q] Conquering Sands, but this is overly restrictive now that there are strong rank up incentives on his [W] Arise! We’re buffing his Mana Growth so he can more freely use his abilities to contest lane.

entries.name: Caitlyn
entries.context: Caitlyn’s been at a very high pick and ban rate for most players for months now despite adjustments to other marksmen and the bot meta, so it's time to nerf her. We have felt that her late-game scaling has been too strong for a while now, so we’re moving some of her power from her eyepopping full build headshots into her early game Q damage to rebalance her power curve.

changes.text: Damage: 60 - 100% AD (+1% AD per 1% per Crit Chance) (+1% AD per 1% Bonus Crit Damage) ⇒ 60 - 80% AD (+0.8% AD per 1% per Crit Chance) (+0.8% AD per 1% Bonus Crit Damage)
changes.label: Damage
changes.before: 60 - 100% AD (+1% AD per 1% per Crit Chance) (+1% AD per 1% Bonus Crit Damage)
changes.after: 60 - 80% AD (+0.8% AD per 1% per Crit Chance) (+0.8% AD per 1% Bonus Crit Damage)

entries.name: Darius
entries.context: Darius has moved a bit too far away from being a persistently durable damage threat that needs to be kited to more of a one shot combo playstyle. Since he has some room for power, we’re giving him a slight boost so he can swing that axe more often in sustained fights.

entries.name: Jinx
entries.context: Like her best friend Caitlyn, Jinx has been similarly dominant in the meta, even with the Hurricane nerf last patch. We’re slowing her roll to make it a tad harder to get her snowballing.

entries.name: Lee Sin
entries.context: Lee Sin has continued to be extremely popular since his adjustments to how his [W] Safeguard cooldown works with allies. While we like the extra flexibility that has given him, it's a bit too much power, so we’re nerfing the cooldown a bit along with a minor bug fix to how his E reveal works against invisible enemies and another small nerf to his [R] Dragon's Rage damage.

changes.text: Bugfix: No longer reveals invisible enemies if they stealth after being hit by Tempest.
changes.label: Bugfix
changes.before: No longer reveals invisible enemies if they stealth after being hit by Tempest.

changes.text: Collision Damage: 175 / 400 / 625 (+200% bonus AD) (+12 / 15 / 18% Kicked Champion's Health) ⇒ 150 / 350 / 550 (+200% bonus AD) (+12 / 15 / 18% Kicked Champion's Health)
changes.label: Collision Damage

entries.name: Locke
entries.context: Locke’s been out for long enough now that we have a better picture of where he’s overly excelling and where he’s falling a bit short. Some of those areas are his extremely generous mana tuning and ability to shrug off harass, and we’re also refining his power curve by improving his scaling damage slightly, because he falls off a bit too fast if he’s not able to close out games early.

changes.text: Unused Charge Refund: 20 - 35% mana and cooldown refund ⇒ 10 - 40% mana and cooldown refund
changes.label: Unused Charge Refund

changes.text: Grey Health Store Based on Current Health: 40 - 200 (both level based) ⇒ 20 - 200
changes.label: Grey Health Store Based on Current Health

changes.text: Current Health Store: 150 - 450 (both level based) ⇒ 100 - 500 (+60% AP)
changes.label: Current Health Store

entries.name: Miss Fortune
entries.context: Miss Fortune has been in a relatively decent place throughout the year, but with the Hubris nerf this patch, we’re looking to compensate with a couple buffs to her damage output.

changes.text: Critical Strike Damage: 130% (+0.3% per 1% Bonus Crit Damage) ⇒ 145% (+0.45% per 1% Bonus Crit Damage)
changes.label: Critical Strike Damage

entries.name: Nidalee
entries.context: Our favorite huntress has been sitting at an extremely high winrate in high skill brackets, toeing the line into overpowered territory for some time now, even if she's not currently meta. Now that we’re bringing down the power of some other powerful meta junglers like Lee Sin, we’re giving Nidalee a minor nerf to prevent her from getting out of paw.

entries.name: Nunu & Willump
entries.context: The boy and his yeti lost some power when we nerfed Hextech Rocketbelt earlier this year so that ranged mages weren't just buying it for a dash to safety, so we’re restoring some of that damage elsewhere.

entries.name: Orianna
entries.context: We’re tapping up Orianna’s scalings to help her chunk a bit harder with her bread-and-butter combo in the late game without giving too much additional power to her laning phase.

entries.name: Qiyana
entries.context: Damage on Qiyana's Q turned out to be a lot more impactful than we anticipated, so we’re partially reverting the buff we gave her back in 26.17.

groups.title: Q - Elemental Wrath / Edge of Ixtal

entries.name: Rammus
entries.context: While Nidalee's winrate has been borderline overpowered in the high skill levels, Rammus has been rolling over pretty much everyone else, so he’s getting a light nerf too, ok?

changes.text: Bonus Magic Resistance: 20 / 25 / 30 / 35 / 40 (+30 - 60% Magic Resistance) ⇒ 20 / 25 / 30 / 35 / 40 (+30 - 50% Magic Resistance)
changes.label: Bonus Magic Resistance

entries.name: Ryze
entries.context: After the significantly early game nerfs to Ryze in 26.19, he hasn't been rewarded enough for succeeding when he does scale, so we’re buffing that.

changes.text: Flux Bonus Damage: 15% / 40% / 65% / 90% increased damage ⇒ 10% / 40% / 70% / 100% increased damage
changes.label: Flux Bonus Damage

entries.name: Sion
entries.context: Our favorite unstoppable juggernaut is looking rather stoppable in recent patches. We’re giving him some buffs to his baseline durability and rewarding him when he succeeds at using his ult to GET IN THERE rather than run away.

changes.text: Damage Increase over the First 3s of Channeling: +0 - 166.67% Base Damage, 0 - 100% Ratio Damage ⇒ +0 - 200%
changes.label: Damage Increase over the First 3s of Channeling

changes.text: Bugfix: Tooltip now displays the correct minimum and maximum bonus AD ratios (40-120%). It displayed an incorrect Bonus AD Scaling (60%-120%). It was never actually changed in patch 25.16 beyond the tooltip.
changes.label: Bugfix
changes.before: Tooltip now displays the correct minimum and maximum bonus AD ratios (40-120%). It displayed an incorrect Bonus AD Scaling (60%-120%). It was never actually changed in patch 25.16 beyond the tooltip.

entries.name: Taliyah
entries.context: Taliyah is one of a handful of mage junglers, and we think she can be better supported for meta diversity. We’re buffing her [E] Unraveled Earth damage to make it more satisfying to land her CC combo.

changes.text: Monster Damage: Deals 225% damage to monsters.
changes.label: Monster Damage

entries.name: Taric
entries.context: We're smoothing out some of the rough edges in Taric’s kit to allow him to shine a bit more. Way back in the day, Taric’s W was adjusted to combat the popular Master Yi + Taric funnel strats. A consequence of this was that his spells would fizzle if they were cast at the same time that his bound ally became untargetable. We believe this harsh restriction to how his abilities function is no longer necessary given the existence of Role Quests, so we're partially reverting this change so that spells now work on untargetable allies, though we are still keeping an existing exemption on [E] Dazzle for champions that disappear on screen because the gameplay is too unclear (sorry, Master Yi).

changes.text: Cast Behavior: Q casts when allies are untargetable will now successfully fire.
changes.label: Cast Behavior
changes.before: Q casts when allies are untargetable will now successfully fire.

changes.text: Cast Behavior: E casts when allies are untargetable will now successfully fire.
changes.label: Cast Behavior
changes.before: E casts when allies are untargetable will now successfully fire.

changes.label: Tooltip
changes.before: Updated to include “Dazzle will not cast from Vanished allies”.

changes.label: Cast Behavior
changes.before: R casts when allies are untargetable will now successfully fire.

entries.name: Tristana
entries.context: Tristana’s early laning has devolved a bit into "Level 1 press [Q] and just auto attack to take complete control of the lane", which is a pretty low gameplay and off flavor way for her to succeed. We’re hitting her early [Q] attack speed so she’ll have to work a bit harder before jumping on her foes.

entries.name: Twisted Fate
entries.context: Alongside the Taric QoL changes, we’re giving Twisted Fate’s R the same treatment so he can reveal champs even if they’re untargetable at the time of activation.

entries.name: Varus
entries.context: In this set of changes, we’re mainly looking to snipe top lane Varus, where he tends to max W, unlike the more common Q max in bot. This won't bring his [Q] Piercing Arrow back up to prior Lethality Varus levels of power, but we believe it will help a lot with our ability to tune him for bot lane. As a maxed ability, it also offers more gameplay to Varus and his opponents to interact with than some more passive damage on W.

entries.name: Vel'Koz
entries.context: Vel’Koz has been a fairly quiet pick this year, having little presence or meta impact in mid and support. We’re looking to give him a little bit of help by rewarding him for landing his combos.

entries.name: Viktor
entries.context: It’s time for the Glorious…Devolution. It seems Viktor has evolved past the point of exploitable weaknesses, so we’re opening that up a bit by making him slightly more vulnerable in early game skirmishes and across the board.

entries.name: Wukong
entries.context: Like Lee and Qiyana, Wukong has been a meta staple whirlwind of a force in the jungle for a while now. We’re looking to tap down his strength in the jungle while compensating for lane Wukong.

changes.text: Armor per Stack: 6 - 10 (based on Champion Level) ⇒ 4.5 - 10 (based on Champion Level)
changes.label: Armor per Stack

entries.name: Xin Zhao
entries.context: Following Sundered Sky's nerfs, we feel like Xin Zhao has room for buffs to both his AD Bruiser and AS focused builds, so we’re helping out his scalings.

changes.text: Damage per Strike: 15 / 30 / 45 / 60 / 75 (+40% bonus AD) ⇒ 15 / 30 / 45 / 60 / 75 (+45% bonus AD)
changes.label: Damage per Strike

changes.label: Attack Speed Scaling

changes.after: 1% per 4% bonus Attack Speed from permanent sources

entries.name: Yone
entries.context: The last changes to Yone successfully got him to start considering crit in his first item purchases, but also put him at a somewhat unsustainable power level. We are giving him a moderate nerf to bring him down a bit.

entries.name: Zyra
entries.context: Like Vel'koz, Zyra has had relatively little impact in the meta as tanks and enchanter supports have reigned supreme. We’re giving Zyra a greener thumb this patch to help her combat the forces trampling over her plants.

entries.name: Bastion Breaker
entries.context: Bastion Breaker was buffed into being a bit of a generic stat stick in order to give it a proper swing in the meta. Now, we’re nerfing that generic power with a QoL improvement to keep it a satisfying item in its niche.

changes.label: Shaped Charge Damage

entries.context: Welcome to the latest ARAM Mayhem release - “Journey to Stardom”. The stars have certainly come out to play as each game of Mayhem will now feature a Headliner performance that applies a unique twist to the rules of each game. Each iconic band will be playing their music while you battle, so make sure you enable your sound and turn up the volume! STAGE CREW ANNOUNCEMENT: It’s taking a little longer to set up the concert stages on Butcher’s Bridge and Koeshin’s Crossing, so expect those maps to be unavailable in Mayhem queues for this patch but return next patch. Along with our Headliners, we have a TON of new augments for you to enjoy. With this release we’ll also be removing some augments and wishing them a fond farewell. But who knows? Maybe they’ll be back some day for an encore. We also have a brand new progression experience where you’ll be completing missions from members K/DA, Pentakill, and other bands. Completing these missions unlocks awesome rewards like Augments, emotes, orange essence, and more! Playing games and completing missions will move you up Superstar Ranks that unlock new bands and new missions. Go from a Newbie to a Superstar performing on the Worlds stage!

entries.context: While we announced that Classic will be rotating out in January, that doesn’t mean we’re done bringing back the good old days this year. This patch we’re bringing in four more ghosts from the past (or more, if you count their ultimates). We’ll also have multiple champions dropping in .22 and .23, so we’ve got a few more historic additions before everything’s all said and done. We’re also reverting all of Kassadin’s nerfs this patch, so he’s back to full 90% ban rate power. And Atma’s Impaler is back to 2%, so for all you Metagolem enjoyers, now’s your time!

entries.name: - Mordekaiser
entries.context: Mordekaiser is back with his kit from 2010-2015! Would you like to eat every single possible minion wave, plus both your and your enemy’s Wraith camps? Mordekaiser is the champion for you. All his abilities cost health, but damaging enemies generates a shield, so you can keep fighting no matter how low you go. And when it’s time to win a fight, your ultimate can turn it into a 6v4. Beat them with their own AD Carry!

changes.text: Mordekaiser converts damage dealt by his abilities into a decaying shield.
Mordekaiser’s next attack damages multiple nearby enemies. If his target is isolated, he deals extra damage to them.
Mordekaiser buffs an ally with a swarm of shrapnel that grants bonus armor and MR and damages nearby enemies over time.
Mordekaiser deals magic damage to enemies in a cone. That’s it. That’s the tooltip.
Mordekaiser curses an enemy champion, dealing damage over time and stealing their stats. If the target dies while cursed, Mordekaiser raises their spirit as a controllable ghost.

entries.name: - Yorick
entries.context: Ghostman yannik cannot compete to mojo style master yu, but he can do the babushka trick to make him double the champion and unleash omen of smell and omen of battle. If that didn’t make any sense to you, you missed out on an all-timer of a forum post. Yorick is back to his original version from 2011-2016, summoning ghouls with every ability he casts and cloning or temporarily reviving his teammates. If you want a quick jumpstart to playing Yorick to his frustratingly immovable best, consider maxing Omen of Famine and getting an early Chalice of Harmony so that you’ll never run out of mana as you constantly drain your opponents and heal while doing so.

changes.text: Yorick takes reduced damage and his attacks deal bonus damage for every summon he has active. This counts his Q, W, E, and R.
Yorick’s next attack deals bonus damage and summons a Spectral Ghoul. Spectral Ghouls have bonus attack damage and movement speed, and give Yorick bonus movement speed while they live.
Yorick summons a Decaying Ghoul in an explosion that damages and slows all nearby enemies. Decaying Ghouls continue to slow enemies around them.
Yorick summons a Ravenous Ghoul, damaging an enemy and healing himself in the process. Ravenous Ghouls heal Yorick every time they attack an enemy.

Yorick conjured the revenant of an allied champion, who can attack for a portion of their total attack damage. If the ally dies while the revenant is active, they are temporarily revived to fight at full power.

entries.name: - Hecarim
entries.context: Hecarim was released in 2012 and hasn’t changed that much over the years, only undergoing some minor mechanical updates to his Q and W. Overall, he goes fast, dives in, and has strong sustained damage while galloping alongside his foes.

changes.text: Hecarim is ghosted and gains Attack Damage based on his bonus Move Speed.
Hecarim cleaves nearby enemies. If he hits an enemy with it, the cooldown of the next cast will be reduced.
Hecarim damages nearby enemies over time and heals based on damage dealt to enemies in the area.
Hecarim gains Move Speed and causes his next attack to deal bonus damage and knock the target back.
Hecarim charges forward, summoning spectral riders that damage enemies they hit. Hecarim inflicts fear on all nearby enemies when ending his charge.

entries.name: - Lucian
entries.context: Lucian is the newest champion to grace League Classic, as he was released in the back half of 2013, but we couldn’t release a bunch of Shadow Isles champions without having our old pal back to keep them in check. There are a few small differences to Lucian here compared to the one you may have played recently. Most notably, he has 550 attack range, which makes him an extremely potent laner.

changes.text: After casting an ability, Lucian’s next attack fires twice.
Lucian fires a piercing shot that damages enemies in a line.
Lucian fires a cross-shaped missile that damages and marks enemies. Damaging marked enemies gives Lucian bonus move speed.
Lucian dashes and removes all slows affecting him. Unlike the modern version of this spell, it doesn’t reset his attack timer and its cooldown is only refreshed by champion kills during his R.
Lucian rapidly fires shots in a straight line. He can move and cast Relentless Pursuit while firing.

entries.name: Aatrox
entries.context: Aatrox isn’t doing so well, especially in top lane, so we’re delivering some level-scaling buffs and overall tankiness buffs to help top lane more than jungle. These are buffs from 2014 and 2015, before his first minor rework in 2017.

entries.name: Irelia
entries.context: Say it with me now, “Better nerf Irelia!” Indeed, she’s come out too powerful, so we’re here to bring her down to size. We’re making her weaker by reverting some buffs from back in 2012, making her less outright durable and forcing her to rely on her high mobility and clever target selection. We’re also adjusting her passive to stack with Mercury Treads like it used to, which is a nerf whenever she builds Tenacity items.

changes.text: Stacking with Tenacity Items: Additive ⇒ Multiplicative
changes.label: Stacking with Tenacity Items

entries.name: Karma
entries.context: Karma is doing poorly, especially in support. As we want her to be viable in both of her primary roles in mid and support, we’re delivering buffs especially skewed toward her low-income role. We’re also delivering a large buff to Spirit Bond, as it can be rather hard to use on teammates.

entries.name: Kassadin
entries.context: Kassadin has continued to be one of the more-banned champions but at this point, it’s clear he just isn’t his old 90% ban rate self. So we’re reverting every nerf we gave him ahead of launch. Go forth and enjoy your full power self! Make your enemies regret leaving him up!

entries.name: Atma's Impaler
entries.context: This patch we’re continuing to relive the glory days by returning peak Atma’s Impaler, as it hasn't had the same impact it historically used to.

Fixed a bug where Sivir’s Spell Shield (E) did not block Ezreal’s Mystic Shot (Q).

entries.context: Welcome back to another Arena patch! This time around we're making a larger set of changes with a couple of goals. We're looking to lower the power level of some of the strongest augments and increase the power of some of the weakest, as well as reduce the sharpness of some of the "one augment combos" so that the champions who're able to high roll with them require a little bit of extra juice to reach their potential. We're also looking to bring some of the champion outliers in power (both high and low) closer to the center. One of the ways we're doing that is through more non-standard changes that allow players the opportunity to use their champions in different ways, and to take advantage of different augments and items. Overall, we've shifted power in ways that we hope will change up the meta a bit and provide some fresh new build options and experiences.

entries.context: As a heads up, during Patch 26.22, we’ll be making changes to the Mythic Shop so that each player will start to see offerings unique to them, rather than everyone having the same selection at a given time. We're hoping this will open up the possibility in the future to allow for you to see more relevant content. In preparation for this, we’ll be making some changes during 26.21 so the rotation timings of the Bi-weekly, Weekly, and Daily sections of the Mythic Shop are better aligned. Keep a close eye on the rotation timings so you don’t miss anything.

We’ve shipped an improvement to how our patch launcher works. This improvement uses a software library that requires SSE 4.2, which results in us increasing our AMD minspec by one version. changes.text: Fixed an issue where Zaahen (Q) would fail to complete if he does into Revive mid attack.
Fixed a bug where Summoner Teleport’s channel VFX was visible for enemies when cast in brush.
Fixed a bug where Titanic Hydra’s cooldown timer would not be displayed after use.
Fixed a bug where Zoe can get a 1000 damage smite from a minion drop earlier than expected.
Fixed a bug where Hail of Blades does not trigger on auto resets if the first attack was cancelled.
Fixed a bug where Nidalee’s (Q) spear damage could go through spell shields at max range.
Updated SFX to use the base skin’s ult SFX for Briar, Kled, and Sion when playing against them to improve clarity.
